card.essence: Poison-ivy. A premier remedy for rheumatic, typhoid and septic states. Affects fibrous tissues (joints, tendons, sheaths) producing tearing pains and marked stiffness. The cardinal feature: symptoms worse on initial motion but ameliorated by continued movement—the patient 'limbers up'. Extreme restlessness drives constant position changes. Suited to ailments from strains, overlifting, or getting wet while perspiring. Characterised by vesicular eruptions, stuporous delirium with triangular red-tipped tongue, and nightly aggravation.

keynotes.text: Lameness, stiffness, pain on FIRST moving after rest, ameliorated by walking or continued motion
Great restlessness; cannot remain in bed; must change position often to obtain relief
Tongue dry, red, cracked with triangular red tip; may be coated except at tip
Ailments from strains, overlifting, getting wet while perspiring, or lying on damp ground
Pains tearing, as if sprained, as if muscle torn from attachment; worse after midnight and wet weather
Great sensitiveness to open air; putting hand from under bedcover brings on cough
Vesicular eruptions with intense itching, burning; erysipelas left to right
Typhoid states: cloudy sensorium, muttering delirium, dry tongue, stupefaction

modalities_worse.text: Beginning motion; initial movement after rest
Cold, wet, rainy weather; before storms; getting wet when perspiring

modalities_better.text: Continued motion; walking about; change of position
Warmth; warm, dry weather; wrapping up; hot applications

mentals: Extreme restlessness, anxiety, apprehension; worse at night; cannot remain in bed
Listless, sad, despondent; thoughts of suicide yet fear of death
Great apprehension at night; fears being poisoned
Delirium: mild, muttering, persistent; continual tossing about
Stupefaction; cloudy sensorium; slow to answer questions
Dreams of great exertion (rowing, swimming, working hard); awakes tired
physicals: Board-like pressure or strapped sensation in forehead; brain feels loose, struck against skull on walking
Scalp sensitive, worse on side lain on; humid itching eruptions
Eyes: swollen, red, oedematous lids agglutinated; profuse hot scalding tears on opening; orbital cellulitis
Tip of nose red, sore, ulcerated; nosebleed on stooping; sneezing, coryza from getting wet
Jaws crack when chewing; easy dislocation of jaw
Corners of mouth ulcerated; fever-blisters around mouth and chin
Parotitis, especially left side
Great thirst with dry mouth and throat; desire for milk; drowsy after eating
Abdomen: violent pains relieved by lying on abdomen; rumbling flatus on first rising, disappears with motion
Diarrhoea: bloody, slimy, reddish mucus; frothy, painless; cadaverous odour; with tearing pains down thighs
Urine dark, turbid, high-coloured, scanty with white sediment
Genitals: swelling with intense itching; scrotum thick, swollen, oedematous; dark-red erysipelatous
Dry teasing cough from midnight until morning, during chill, or when putting hands out of bed
Haemoptysis from overexertion; blood bright red
Hoarseness from overstraining voice
Heart: hypertrophy from overexertion; numbness/aching in left arm; palpitation better from motion
Back: pain between shoulders on swallowing; pain and stiffness in small of back worse sitting/lying, better motion
Stiff neck; interscapular pain worse swallowing
Sciatica left side; pains down back of thighs worse during stool
Legs feel dead, wooden; cramp in calves
Palms dry, hot, cracked, sore; washing causes burning
Skin: vesicular, crusty, eczematous eruptions; erysipelas left to right; intense itching, burning worse warmth
Cellulitis; carbuncles in early stages; septic conditions
clinical: Rheumatic conditions: fibrous tissue, joints, tendons; worse cold damp weather, better continued motion
Typhoid fever with triangular red-tipped tongue, restlessness, stupefaction
Influenza with aching in all bones
Erysipelas: vesicular, left to right progression, with characteristic restlessness
Scarlatina with vesicular eruption and restlessness
Infantile paralysis from exposure to cold damp ground
Hypertrophy of heart from overexertion in athletes, machinists
Intermittent, remittent fevers with restlessness and characteristic tongue
Old injured eyes; iritis from cold, damp exposure

differentials.note: Complementary. Bryonia worse any motion, wants absolute rest; Rhus worse initial motion, better continued movement. Bryonia dry mucous membranes, wants large drinks; both have typhoid states.
Both intensely restless, but Arsenicum from anxiety/fear, worse after midnight, with profound prostration; Rhus restlessness from pain seeking relief in motion. Both in typhoid states.
Both restless, but Aconite's is agonising with intense fear, no relief from position changes; Rhus relieved temporarily by movement. Aconite seldom in typhoid.
Inimical—must not be used before or after Rhus. Both have oedema, but Apis ameliorated by cold, worse warmth; Rhus opposite.
Both in typhoid with stupefaction and sore bruised feeling, but Baptisia more profound mental confusion, falls asleep mid-sentence; less restlessness than Rhus.
Similar stupefaction in typhoid, but Nux moschata has extreme drowsiness, dryness of mouth without thirst; Rhus has great thirst.
Sepia often quickly ameliorates itching and burning of Rhus vesicles, drying them up in a few days.

cautions: Inimical to Apis—must not be used before or after
Dermatitis from Rhus should never be treated by topical medicated applications; they suppress, never cure; use potentised remedy internally
Continued exertion exhausts the Rhus patient despite initial amelioration from motion
In heart hypertrophy, must be given persistently for days or weeks to effect absorption of surplus cardiac muscle
